result:
{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I proposed the fish in the first minute because the forked tail makes it recognizable from the outline alone. I sketched the pad, with one run from the nose that splits into top and bottom lines and a big tail fin. That plan gave everyone a clear job right away. By the final check about 153 of 157 dominoes were connected to the start. Four dominoes in the middle of the fin's back edge never joined the chain. We chose to leave them because the outline was complete without them. I can't say how the judge will read the fish, but the shape matches the sketch.

**Execution:** I laid stroke 1 (the start and nose) and the top body line, then inspected the chain and closed a small gap where the body meets the tail. When Hana's top fin piece drifted out and stayed disconnected, I took it over and re-laid it from the pad. A gap near the top of the fin then showed up, and Hana spotted it before I did. I fixed it, and that fin got finished later than I wanted. I also had to accept a loose stub at the end instead of getting a perfect build. I never bumped anyone. Jack's bump near Omar was the only one.

**Collaboration:** I split the work by line so people stayed out of each other's way, and I kept the table updated. Omar's inspections and Hana's gap-spotting caught real problems. Taking over Hana's fin piece was the right call for time, but I should have asked her first and offered her a different job sooner. I deferred to Jack on leaving the stub alone and to the group on staying hands-off.

**Leadership:** I made the early decisions (animal, pad layout, who builds which stroke) and kept status updates short and accurate for you. I did not overstate the result. The remaining stub was reported as a stub."}
